sections.h2: Who lives in Pike County, and how does that shape a sale?
sections.html:
Pike County grew from 17,869 people in 2010 to 18,889 in the 2020 census, and the estimate for July 2025 stands at 20,932. Pike's 10.8% gain since the 2020 base is the steepest among the four counties in the bureau's table. Zebulon is the seat, and the county tax commissioner keeps an office at 79 Jackson Street there.

The households are family-sized: 2.92 people each, with 23.2% of residents under 18. Owners hold 84.6% of homes, and 91.6% of residents stayed put for the previous year. People who commute leave early, since the mean trip to work takes 35.7 minutes. Only 1.7% of residents were born abroad, and 1,251 are veterans.

Spending patterns tell you where buyers shop. Retail sales in 2022 came to $78,480,000, only $3,933 per resident, so much of the buying power goes to other counties. The county employs 2,279 people at 332 employer establishments, while 2,060 businesses have no employees at all.

sections.h2: What do Pike County home prices and incomes look like?
sections.html:
A home occupied by its owner has a middle value of $305,600, and a middle household takes in $86,719. Both are the top figures in the four-county table.

Monthly owner costs have a median of $1,869 with a mortgage and $605 without. Poverty touches 8.4% of residents. At those home values, the yearly tax bill is a meaningful payoff line, and a missed one grows quickly under the penalty schedule described below.

sections.h2: What do Pike County's jobs and internet numbers say about buyers?
sections.html:
Pike's buyers tend to be working households with commutes. The labor force takes in 60.3% of residents over 16, and 55.3% of women over 16 are in it. Employment at county employers rose 9.5% between 2022 and 2023, on a 2023 payroll of $93,756,000.

Connectivity helps a remote worker consider the county. In 2020-2024, 94.4% of households had a computer and 84.6% had a broadband subscription. High school completion for adults 25 and over is 89.2%.

Land is not scarce, yet density is rising. The county counted 82.7 people per square mile in 2010 and 87.4 in 2020, across 216.09 square miles. Health coverage is a weak spot: 12.4% of residents under 65 lack insurance, and 7.4% have a disability.

A seller can use these numbers when pricing. Buyers with higher incomes and long drives expect a well kept house, and a listing with an open tax lien or unfinished repairs gives them a reason to wait.

sections.h2: Which Pike County office should I call?
sections.html:
Call the tax commissioner about a bill and the assessors about a value. The two numbers are one digit apart.

  • Tax commissioner: (770) 567-2001, weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00. Online payments run through pikecountypay.com.
  • Tax assessors: (770) 567-2002 for returns, homestead forms, valuation and appeals.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: deed room at the county courthouse, and the place where a tax lien is recorded.
  • City of Zebulon: its website says Pike County bills city property tax for it, so there is no second counter for city residents.

The office states that bills are addressed to the owner. A lender holding an escrow account will not receive one, so pass your copy along.

sections.h2: What does a late Pike County bill cost?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property bills fall due December 1. A mobile home bill is due April 1. Postmarks from the United States Postal Service count, and a metered mark does not.

The county writes its penalty schedule in four steps:

  1. Interest posts on the 2nd of every month at prime plus 3%, divided by 12.
  2. A 5% penalty is added at 120 days, then again every 120 days, capped at 20%.
  3. Thirty days past the delinquent notice date, a FIFA is filed in the Clerk of Courts office.
  4. The account then moves to a contractor, and fees of $215 plus can be added for certified mail and a title search before the sale.

A mobile home takes a 10% penalty starting April 2. In the weeks before an auction the parcel is posted, photographed and advertised in the local paper for four weeks.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Pike County valuation?
sections.html:
Write to the assessors inside 45 days of the notice date. The county says an appeal sent after that cutoff cannot be accepted.

Argue one of three things: the property is not taxable, the value is wrong, or the value is out of line with similar parcels. A complaint that the tax amount is too high will not work, because millage is a separate decision. Should the assessors stand by their number, a hearing before the Board of Equalization follows, or arbitration if you prefer. Superior Court is the last stop.

Mobile home owners follow a shorter chain: 45 days with the assessors, then 21 days to reach the Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: What lowers a Pike County tax bill?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption is the first thing to check. You need to own and occupy the house on January 1, and the assessors must receive your form before April 1.

  • The assessors ask first-time filers to show their deed.
  • Pike adds its own county exemption amounts, and the bigger of the local and state figures applies.
  • Age 62 opens an extra exemption.
  • Working farmland may be taxed on 30% of market value, and conservation land on its use value. Both need a covenant of at least a decade.
  • Manufacturers can seek the freeport exemption in the January 1 to April 1 window.

The exemption continues from year to year until the home, its owner or the kind of exemption changes.

sections.h2: How is a Pike County bill built?
sections.html:
Taxable value is 40% of market value as of January 1, less exemptions. Rates come from the county commissioners and the school board separately. Each mill levies $1 on $1,000 of taxable value.

Returns follow a pattern. A real estate return is needed only after a purchase or an improvement, and it is filed January 1 through April 1. A required return that never gets filed draws a 10% charge on whatever value was left off. Equipment and other personal property goes on a fresh return every year.

sections.h2: How should I sell a Pike County house that has unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Collect a written payoff and have the closing attorney deduct it at the table. Interest keeps growing monthly, so the number changes with the calendar.

  1. Phone (770) 567-2001 for the amount owed and any penalty.
  2. Ask whether a FIFA exists and what clears it.
  3. If the account is at the contractor stage, request the extra fees as a separate line.
  4. Check which year's bill falls on you under the contract.

Closing before the tax sale stage avoids newspaper and levy costs. When repairs or an inherited deed are the holdup, an as-is purchase lets you pick a closing date around them.

faqs.q: Which date should I use for the Pike County bill?
faqs.a: December 1 for real estate. The county tax site gives that date, even though the state default is December 20.

faqs.q: How fast does Pike County add penalties?
faqs.a: Interest posts monthly, the first 5% penalty comes at 120 days, and the cap is 20%. Mobile homes get 10% on April 2.

faqs.q: Which Pike County office takes a homestead form?
faqs.a: The tax assessors, and it must be in hand before April 1. First-time homeowners should carry the deed.

faqs.q: Will a recorded FIFA stop a Pike County sale?
faqs.a: No. It is a lien that gets paid out of the proceeds. Ask the tax commissioner at (770) 567-2001 what the payoff is.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about my Pike County value?
faqs.a: The assessors at (770) 567-2002. Billing and payment go to the commissioner at (770) 567-2001.
